purpose: Fentanyl is used to treat severe pain that cannot be controlled by other pain medicines. It is often used for cancer pain, post-surgical pain, or chronic pain in people who are already used to taking strong opioid medicines. Some forms are used for sudden breakthrough pain that comes on quickly and intensely.
how_it_works: Fentanyl works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord called opioid receptors. When it attaches to these receptors, it blocks pain signals from reaching your brain, so you feel less pain. It is very powerful — much stronger than morphine — so even a small amount has a strong effect on your body.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, nausea or upset stomach, constipation, headache, confusion or difficulty concentrating, dry mouth, and itching or sweating. You may also feel a sense of relaxation or euphoria.
warnings: Fentanyl is extremely powerful and can be life-threatening if misused. It can slow down or stop your breathing, which can be fatal — especially if taken by someone who has not been prescribed it. Never share this medication with anyone. Do not drink alcohol or take other sedatives with it. Keep all forms of fentanyl locked away and out of reach of children — even a small amount can kill a child. Fentanyl can be habit-forming, and stopping it suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms. Always talk to your doctor before changing your dose or stopping.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the form prescribed. Skin patches (like Duragesic) are usually changed every 72 hours and come in different strengths based on your pain needs. Lozenges or dissolving tablets for breakthrough pain are used as needed when sudden pain hits. Doses are carefully chosen by your doctor based on how much opioid pain medicine your body is already used to. Never adjust your dose on your own.
